newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso gains ground as turnover swells.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso gains ground as turnover swells.

text.p: The Philippine peso recovered to 26.376 to the dollar by mid-afternoon as banks started to sell dollars after the Central Bank kept its selling rate firm at 26.379, traders said.
The peso was hovering at 26.379 by midday, after falling to 26.380 in the morning following speculative attacks on regional currencies.
Turnover in the foreign exchange market swelled to a record $925.20 million with traders dealing value-spot or settlement on Monday in the afternoon.
In the local market, trades done in the forex market are settled the next working day.
Value-spot deals are settled two working days after the deal. The U.S. market is closed on Friday for the Independence Day.
Deals to be settled on Monday were hovering between 26.405 and 26.407 due to the large swap points during the long weekend.
Traders said foreign banks had started to unload some of the dollars they bought in the morning due to the high interest rate premium offered by peso-denominated instruments.
"The market has calmed down," one trader said.
